lines.text: Many learners say: I arrived to the station.
Better: I arrived at the station.
Arrive goes with at, not to.
At! I arrived at the station.

data.why: Arrive goes with at, not to.

native.hook: 「到着する」に to を使ってない？
native.tip: arrive の後ろは at（建物・駅）か in（都市）。to は使いません。
native.caption: “I arrived to the station.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「に」につられて to を使いがち。arrive の後は at を使います。 “I arrived at the station.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“at”。arrive のあとは at か in。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: After arrive, use at for places or in for cities. Not to.
en.caption: Do you say “I arrived to the station.”? 😅 The Japanese “ni” pulls you to use to, but after arrive you say at. The natural way is “I arrived at the station.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
